title: Watchman: SSE/WebSocket latency & tokens/sec regression harness for streaming chat
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a scalable, reproducible load-testing harness ("Watchman") for SSE and WebSocket streaming chat/completions that focuses on tokens/sec throughput, end-to-end p95 latency, and automated regression detection. This harness must: simulate realistic client mixes with per-session token pacing and prefix/KV-cache behavior, run continuous baselines against staging + dedicated pools, export high-cardinality telemetry (per-tenant, per-model, per-route), and surface regressions to alerting and PR workflows.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run 10k concurrent streaming sessions (SSE + WS) from a distributed runner cluster and reproduce workload profiles
Dashboard shows tokens/sec (global & per-model), e2e p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, connection churn metrics, and KV-cache hit rate
Automated regression detector triggers alerts when p95 increases by >10% vs 7-day baseline and creates a starter GitHub issue with attached CSV traces
Integrations: Grafana dashboard (read-only), PagerDuty + #infra-load Slack alerts, and a daily baseline report generated to S3
Per-route and per-tenant telemetry exported to our observability pipeline with stable tag names to enable long-term trend analysis
technical_notes: Architecture: controller/orchestrator that schedules worker pods across regions; workers are protocol adapters (SSE/WS) with a small embedded runtime client to exercise server endpoints
Client mix: sampled user archetypes (short-chats, long-context, streaming-incremental) with configurable token pacing distributions (Poisson and bursty Pareto) to simulate real traffic
KV-cache model: session affinity + simulated prefix cache hits using deterministic prefix buckets to exercise cache-aware paths in the runtime
Metrics: per-session token emission rate, token ack latency, buffer build-up time, p95 end-to-end (time from first request bytes to final newline chunk), connection setup time, and reconnect rate

Regression detection: two-stage detector — short-term EWMA anomaly gate + longer-term change-point analysis (CUSUM) on p95 and tokens/sec; false positives reduced via coordinated baselines and traffic weighting
Data retention: raw traces archived to s3://redwood-bench-results/watchman/YYYY-MM-DD/; summary metrics forwarded to metrics cluster with labels {model, route, region, tenant_tier}
Resource model: harness supports GPU-backed model stubs for controlled injections and can replay against staging-dedicated or a lightweight stub for load-only tests
Safety: rate-limits at harness to avoid accidental blast on production; runbook included for graceful abort and for returning clusters to baseline
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Kickoff and RFC accepted by Serving Performance. Defined success criteria and telemetry schema.

2026-02-28: First end-to-end run against staging-dedicated: 1k concurrent sessions, identified a 15% regression in p95 when enabling KV cache emulation (investigating).
2026-03-03: Integrated stats exporter to telemetry pipeline (metrics prefix: load.watchman.*). Baseline job scheduled nightly.
2026-03-07: Built Grafana dashboard (read-only link below). Added tokens/sec heatmap and p95 trend panel. Initial thresholds tuned to reduce noise.
2026-03-10: Implemented CUSUM-based change detector and validate on historical traces — reduced false positives by ~60% in synthetic regressions.
2026-03-12: Created GitHub prototype PR for harness infra and test runners (link below). Running 5-day soak in staging to collect baseline.
2026-03-14: PM requested experiment knobs for per-tenant weighting and a lightweight mode that runs without model stubs. Planning rollout for canary alerts next week.
